questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Stop them from riding any way you can. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: When braking, which brake should you use?

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes at the same time.
Either brake, but never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together to stop. Using both brakes at the same time gives you the best braking power.

questions.question: If you are drinking and plan to ride later, what should you do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than usual.
Wait at least one hour for each drink to leave your body before riding.
Exercise or dance to get the alcohol out of your system.
Drink hot coffee to stay alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait at least one hour for each drink to leave your body before riding.
questions.explanation: The only way to get alcohol out of your system is to wait. Your body removes about one drink per hour. Riding after drinking is dangerous, even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding on a paved road with sand and gravel, what should you do?

options.text: Shift down and use more throttle.
Pull in the clutch.
Use only the rear brake to slow down.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces like sand and gravel, avoid sudden changes in speed or direction. Be extra careful on surfaces with poor traction.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than you would alone.
Use only the front brake.
Never talk to them.
Start in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than you would alone.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This means it takes longer to slow down. Begin braking sooner when you have a passenger than when riding alone.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
Are usually minimal.
Often cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can make it unsafe to ride. Mixing drugs with alcohol can make their effects even more dangerous.

questions.question: During a pre-ride check, what should you verify about your brakes?

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes create friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and can hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: What is the best way to be seen at night?

options.text: Wear light-colored clothing.
Wear a white helmet.
Wear reflective clothing.
Wear a red jacket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: To be most visible at night, wear bright clothing with reflective materials.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, what is the best approach?

options.text: Signal, check your left mirror, look left, and move into the passing lane.
Signal and immediately move into the passing lane while accelerating.
Signal, check your left mirror, and move into the passing lane.
Signal, accelerate, and move into the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your left mirror, look left, and move into the passing lane.
questions.explanation: To pass safely, signal first. Check your left mirror and turn your head to look left. When it is clear, move to the passing lane and accelerate quickly. Pass through the other vehicle's blind spot as fast as possible. Then signal again, check your mirrors, and look back before returning to your original lane.

questions.question: For the most safety, how should your helmet fit?

options.text: Tight at the base and loose at the top.
Loose all the way around.
Snug all the way around.
Wear it only on long rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug all the way around.
questions.explanation: Your helmet should fit snug all the way around. Wear a helmet every time you ride. Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Protects you in a crash.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: You should wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding. Leather protects you in a crash. Even in warm weather, many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: The proper body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
Lets you sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the handle grips.
Makes you lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keeps your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handle grips. This lets you easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, you should be able to see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane behind you.
Only the lane next to you.
Most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. The road behind and to the side of you is most important.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Take the owner's word that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Check the controls and gear pattern before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Polyester
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while turning or on a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten the motorcycle first, then brake.
Brake first, then try to straighten the motorcycle.
Only brake and not worry about straightening.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the motorcycle first, then brake.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly while turning or on a curve, straighten the motorcycle first and then brake. Motorcycles have less traction when leaning in a turn.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothes should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for proper protection.

questions.question: For the most protection, choose a helmet that:

options.text: Fits loosely.
Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Has survived a previous crash.
Provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: Which of these should you check during a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion on your seat
The shine of your paint
The wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.
